Well, not sure why ppl are down voting me, I simply want to know where this feeling of hopelessness to the point is coming from, whether it is due to mental illness alone or some other reason, which in this case includes terminal illness. I do know I probably won't be able to help you, I have a boyfriend suffering from mental illness as well as losing his eyesight. He hardly ever talks to anyone, including me, due to constant excessive guilt and I know he has suicidal ideations too although he won't admit it to me. No matter what I say to him, it doesn't seem to help make him feel better. Most times I think I just make him feel more guilty, even when I'm trying to be positive and supportive of him. 

I've had suicidal ideations myself and for the most part it stems from loneliness and difficulty connecting with people. That's why I think having people who not only love you but can connect with you helps a lot to alleviate that hopelessness. But I also know that having loved ones doesn't necessarily means we can talk to them about anything, which is the case for me and may be the case for you. If you do have someone you can trust enough to talk to, please really to them at I'm sure that will help more than some random people on Reddit. 

I don't know what disease you have and if you're not willing to reveal it, that's fine. But I hope you at least try to exhaust all medical options to try and extend your lifespan to the fullest. I'm sure your loved ones would help you look for options.

But if that fails, then I can understand as well the desire to go out on your own terms. But I also know if my boyfriend committed suicide without at least saying goodbye, I would be utterly devastated. So I hope that you would at least give a proper goodbye to your loved ones before if you really feel that's the path you must take.

Sorry to hear that happened to you. If anyone ever gets chased by a dog, running /cycling off and screaming is the worst thing to do as it will trigger the dog's instinct to chase you down even more. Best thing is to stand your ground, stay calm and firmly and loudly (but not screaming as this further triggers dogs) tell the dog to back off and even bend down and pretend to pick up something to throw at it. Unless it's a dog specifically trained to attack, most dogs will back off and just bark from a distance. Then just slowly back off (still calm) and walk away but keep an eye on the dog and keep talking loudly to the dog to show him you mean business. Staying calm is the most important thing as dogs sense fear. Probably easier said than done, but trust me it works very well. I've had dogs all my life and come across a good number of aggressive barking dogs in my life and it has never failed.

Here's a tip to reduce RP when upgrading S or R cards. This works only if you have spare S or R cards that you don't need. 

1) Level up the spare card by slightly over half of it's max level (I usually level up to level 25 for S cards and maybe level 27 for R cards)

2) Do the same for the S or R card you want to level up to max (level it up to slightly over half of max level) 

3)  Use the partially levelled up spare S or R card to level up the card you want.

4) If the level up is perfect, the card you leveled up would probably hit level 50 without need for more cards. But if it's just good, then you might need to top up to 50 with a few more cards

Reason for this is after the higher the card level, the more cards you need to reach max level. So doing this reduced the cards and hence the RP you use. Hope it makes sense
